components.goal: Apply the prescribed gradient update using a dimensionless parameter h.

components.name: Constant normalized gradient step
components.operation: Compute x-(h/L)grad f(x) after one exact oracle query.
components.requires: Public positive L and fixed h; full exact gradient.

content.family: Fixed-step gradient descent; the radial Huber construction is a worst-instance witness, not the algorithm family.

limitations.statement: Theorem 3.2 challenges only this fixed-step recurrence and x_N output.

Theorem 3.1 asserts an upper bound for 0<h<=1. The upper candidate uses a separate local weak-duality derivation for the p11 step, awaiting independent review. This Algorithm has no structured scientific dependence on that candidate.
The max-formula upper bound for all 0<h<2 is Conjecture 3.1 in this artifact. Its optimal-step discussion is conditional.

performance_links.scope_note: Existential instance for the prescribed h,N and last iterate; every h>0. Not an all-algorithms lower bound.

variants.cost: N first-order oracle calls at x0,...,x_(N-1). An optional query to observe f(x_N) is additional and is not required to produce the output. Each update also performs vector scaling/subtraction in R^d; a direct implementation uses O(d) arithmetic per update and O(d) working storage, excluding oracle-internal computation. These implementation counts are separate from the source oracle-call metric.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF p5 Algorithm GM; standing model p4
variants.name: Algorithm GM
variants.output: Return x_N, without averaging or selecting a best-value iterate.
variants.query_and_update: For i=0,...,N-1, query at x_i, receive (f(x_i),g_i) with g_i=grad f(x_i), and set x_(i+1)=x_i-(h/L)g_i. Function values are not used by this recurrence.
variants.requirements: Unconstrained Euclidean R^d; f convex, C^1, with globally L-Lipschitz gradient. Exact first-order oracle returns function value and full gradient at queried x.
variants.state_and_initialization: Store x=x0. The standing performance model promises a minimizer within distance R>0; neither x* nor f* is required to run the updates.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Choose h>0 before the run and keep it fixed. Stop after exactly N updates. R is unnecessary for a fixed-budget execution. The source's upper statement is for 0<h<=1; its corrected candidate awaits independent review. No line search or restart is specified.
